taskVersion.name: ves-heldout-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station H-01, survey area H. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 332.5 | 0.52 | 0.52
2 | 601.3 | 6.89 | 7.41
3 | 359.9 | 16.01 | 23.42
4 | 286.0 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as K-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station H-01, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

Station H-01 (Survey Area H) consists of a four-layer sequence with resistivities of 332.5 ohm-m, 601.3 ohm-m, 359.9 ohm-m, and 286.0 ohm-m.

Applying the provided curve-type notation rules:
- The first triplet (layers 1-2-3) follows the $r_1 < r_2 > r_3$ pattern, which is K.
- The second triplet (layers 2-3-4) follows the $r_2 > r_3 > r_4$ pattern, which is Q.

The correct notation for this four-layer curve is KQ. The classification on file as "K-type" is incorrect; according to the rules, a four-layer curve must be represented by two letters unless they are identical (in which case a single letter may be used). Because the sequence is KQ and not KK, the single-letter classification is invalid.

{"curve_type_stated": "K", "label_issue_flagged": true}
